title: What If Another Tambora Erupted Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if the volcano that cancelled summer erupted again tomorrow?
In 1815, Tambora in Indonesia erupted at VEI seven, throwing out at least thirty-seven cubic kilometers of material. It was the biggest in at least thirteen hundred years.
Explosions were heard about eighteen hundred kilometers away, and ash fell hundreds of miles from the mountain.
Its sulfur aerosols dimmed the sun, and average global temperatures dropped by roughly half a degree Celsius.
In June of 1816, snow fell in Albany, New York, and frost wrecked crops across the northeastern United States.
Europe suffered its worst famine of the century. Tambora is still the most recent eruption of that size.

description:
What if another Tambora erupted tomorrow?
The 1815 eruption in Indonesia dimmed the sun, dropped temperatures and caused the Year Without a Summer. It is still the most recent VEI 7 eruption.
What should we run through next?
